summary_hint: {court} decree, {petitioner} v. {respondent}, {decree_status}, entered {decree_entry_date}, {N} support obligations, {N} property/debt awards.

typed_core.name: decree_entry_date
typed_core.why: identity — when the decree was entered (the effective date)

typed_core.name: decree_final_date
typed_core.why: disambiguator — final/effective date vs entry date

typed_core.name: decree_status
typed_core.why: processor — final vs interlocutory/pending; an unfinalized decree can't be relied on
typed_core.prompt_hint: Distinguish final vs interlocutory — only a final decree is reliable

typed_core.name: dissolution_granted_indicator
typed_core.why: processor — is the divorce actually granted

typed_core.name: name_change_order
typed_core.why: processor — name matching across the loan file

typed_core.name: incorporated_settlement_agreement
typed_core.why: disambiguator — support/property terms may live in an incorporated MSA, not the decree body

nested_lists.name: support_obligations
nested_lists.shape_reason: the single highest-value structure — each obligation is income for one party and a liability for the other. Few items (1-4), flat is cheap. The one budgeted nested list

fields.name: obligation_type
fields.why: alimony vs child support — never merge the two

fields.name: frequency
fields.why: per month / monthly / schedule — makes the amount readable

fields.name: payer
fields.why: who pays — the same amount is income to one party and a liability to the other

fields.name: recipient
fields.why: who receives — added alongside payer so direction is unambiguous

fields.name: source
fields.why: provenance snippet for the obligation row

rejected.name: issuer_name, issuer_address/phone/email
rejected.reason: issuer is the court, captured by court_name

rejected.name: property_address, loan_number, account_case_reference_number
rejected.reason: property captured in real_property_awards; no loan link

rejected.name: clerk_filing_stamp, amendment_or_modification_orders, retirement_or_qdro_provisions, personal_property_awards, equalization_or_lump_sum_payment, childcare_or_other_recurring_obligations
rejected.reason: low-frequency / no consumer -> catch-all (revisit if a DTI rule needs them)

encoding_variations: Support is stated as '$X per month', '$X monthly', or a schedule; capture amount + frequency and the payer so the direction (income vs liability) is unambiguous
Parties appear as 'Petitioner/Respondent' or 'Plaintiff/Defendant' — normalize by role, keep raw names
Key financial terms are often in an incorporated marital settlement agreement rather than the decree text — incorporated_settlement_agreement flags when obligations may be off-page

open_questions.q: Second and third nested lists. The domain arguably needs three repeating structures (support, debt, property); the standard budgets one per document absent rules.
options: (c) ship all three (matching/exceeding the existing extractor's two)
open_questions.recommendation: (b) — support_obligations plus one merged asset/debt-allocation list, since the existing extractor already carries two lists and debt allocation drives DTI

open_questions.q: payer/recipient labeling. Obligations reference 'Petitioner/Respondent' or names.
open_questions.recommendation: capture both the raw label and the resolved name so direction is auditable

open_questions.q: case_number PII class. Confidential but not SSN-class. Register in _PII_FIELDS or keep as a plain typed field?
options: keep as a plain typed field

notes: No rules consume this type today, so there is no rule floor.

An existing starter extractor ships (3-field typed core); all three are retained (renamed): party_1_name -> petitioner_name, party_2_name -> respondent_name, effective_date -> decree_entry_date. The support_obligations and property_awards nested lists already ship (add a recipient field to support_obligations).
ADD fields a rule/processor needs, today only in the unmasked catch-all: case_number, decree_status, debt_allocations (nested), court_name/court_jurisdiction, dissolution_granted_indicator.
case_number is confidential but not SSN-class; kept as a plain typed field and flagged for review rather than auto-registering in _PII_FIELDS.
Prompt hint (support obligations are the priority): capture every obligation as its own list entry; never merge alimony and child support.
Prompt hint (payer): record who pays each obligation (a name or party label) — the same $1,200/mo is income to one borrower and a liability to another.
judge_name's why cites 'execution', which is not one of the five reason_class values; mapped to processor and flagged as an ambiguity.
